result:
The worker fixed all six round-1 defects — genuinely, and [1.1] at the root rather than by disclosure. But the rewrite introduced a new false claim.

## Round-1 defects: all fixed, all verified

**[1.1]** The worker didn't take my "no re-run required" escape. It ran a real token-matched control (DeepWalk ×15 = 104,370 walks = 4,174,800 tokens, +2.6% over U-U-U-A-U) and re-anchored Table 2 and both figures on it. Its `corpus_size.json` matches my round-1 measurement on every field. The headline is now reported against both controls (+0.0045 vs token-matched, −0.0016 vs walk-matched) — a stronger null than either alone.

**[1.2]** Mid-walk truncation is now documented with the mechanism and the measured lengths (24.3/27.5, 32.2%/43.7% full). **[1.3]–[1.6]** all fixed; still 6 pages despite the added content, and the figures survived the height reduction.

I re-verified independently: all 14×8 Table 1 cells, all 6×8 Table 2 cells against the new reference column, the new 14-row noise floor, all 20 bolded cells (including the subtle 8–15 row where H@1 and MRR bold different columns), and every delta to full precision.

## The new defect

`answer.tex:245–250` now claims: *"the scaffolding breaks ties at random, so an all-zero row scores exactly chance, 1/21 = 0.0476 — and chance is what all three social-only configurations measure... the spread between them is tie-breaking noise."*

I trained the embedding and looked at the actual scores:

- **0 of 216** cold-source queries have tied scores. Median 20 distinct scores out of 21; spread 2.12–5.33. The source row *is* all-zero, but `_pair_features` still emits `|u−v| = |v|` and `‖u−v‖ = ‖v‖`, which vary by candidate — so the predictor ranks on candidate-only features.
- **Tie-breaking contributes zero variance.** `evaluate_ranking` seeds with a constant and is never passed a seed, so the tiebreak vector is byte-identical in every run. This is self-disproving from the worker's own data: tied scores + identical tiebreaks would force identical cold hit@1 across seeds, yet they differ (0.0880/0.0972/0.0556).
- **×15 isn't at chance** — 0.0803 is +3.9 sd above 1/21. Cold MRR 0.2210 vs chance 0.1736 says the same.

My run reproduces the worker's ×15 seed-0 cold value exactly (0.0880), so this is the same quantity.

The cold-start *result* is untouched — 0.28/0.36 against any baseline in 0.045–0.080 is a 3.5–8× effect. What fails is the asserted mechanism, and the "5.9× / 7.6× chance" and "8.7 / 11.5 sd" figures that rest on it. Round 1's version anchored on the measured control and was fine; this replaced a control-dependent truth with an unmeasured falsehood. Fix is confined to one paragraph, two sentences, and two figure labels — no re-running.

Plus two minors: `float` is now unused (same class as the `enumitem` item just fixed), and `submission.md` preserves the wrong justification.

VERDICT: FAIL
